title: Cases, queues, assignment rules, escalation rules, auto-response, email-to-case, and web-to-case
objectives: Define Case as the support work record and Queue as shared ownership, not a user.
Distinguish assignment rules, escalation rules, and auto-response rules by when they fire and what they change.
Explain Email-to-Case and Web-to-Case as capture channels that still need an active assignment rule or Support Settings default owner.
Troubleshoot a case that landed on the default owner or never emailed the customer.
diagnostic_question: A customer emails support@, another uses a website form, and a VIP case has sat 4 hours. Which of queue, assignment rule, escalation rule, auto-response, Email-to-Case, or Web-to-Case do you inspect first for each, and what evidence would change your choice?
definition: Service Cloud capture and first-line routing: a Case is the work record; Queues hold cases for a team; assignment rules route new cases to a user or queue; auto-response rules email the customer at create; escalation rules reassign or notify after time; Email-to-Case and Web-to-Case create cases from inbound channels. If no active assignment rule matches, Support Settings default owner receives the case. ([Assignment Rules for IT Services](https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=service.it_srvcs_assignment_rules.htm) describes user-or-queue routing and one active rule per object in that product; classic Case assignment follows the same user-or-queue idea—reverify the Case-specific Help article in the org.)
why_it_matters: Interviewers fail people who use a Flow for every inbound email, who confuse auto-response with escalation, or who forget the default case owner. Web-to-Case is first submission only; it is not a portal. Exceeding the daily Web-to-Case limit emails leftover details to the default owner rather than silently creating unlimited cases.
sixty_second_explanation: Picture a hospital ER. The Case is the patient chart. A Queue is a shared waiting bay, not a doctor. Assignment rules are triage protocols that send a new chart to a bay or a named clinician. Auto-response is the 'we have your intake' text. Escalation is the timeout pager when the chart sits too long. Email-to-Case is a faxed referral becoming a chart; Web-to-Case is the kiosk form. The default owner is the charge nurse when triage rules miss.
deeper_explanation: Assignment rules evaluate record attributes and assign to a user or a queue. You can have multiple rules defined, but only one assignment rule can be active at a time for an object in the IT Services Help. Apply the same 'active rule' discipline to Case assignment: inactive rules send web or email cases to the default owner in Support Settings. ([Assignment Rules for IT Services](https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=service.it_srvcs_assignment_rules.htm))

Web-to-Case is solely a tool for initial submission. If customers must track or update cases, use an authenticated experience (Experience Cloud / self-service), not another HTML form. Before setup: case queues, Support Settings default owner, an active assignment rule, and an email template for notification. If the org exceeds its daily Web-to-Case limit, the default case owner receives an email with the extra case information. (Needs verification of the numeric daily cap in current Case Help—do not invent a number.)

Email-to-Case turns inbound messages into Cases (On-Demand Email-to-Case versus Email-to-Case with an agent is a setup choice—reverify current Help). Routing addresses, attachments, and threading behave differently from Web-to-Case's anonymous form post.

Auto-response rules send email when a case is created and criteria match—they do not reassign. Escalation rules are time-dependent: they notify, reassign, or otherwise act after business hours elapse. Entitlement milestones (APP-004) are a different SLA clock.
Queues are metadata (members, supported objects). Case rows are data. Do not treat a Queue as a User in reports without using the queue OwnerId.

mental_model.analogy: A hospital ER: Case = patient chart; Queue = shared waiting bay; assignment rule = triage protocol; auto-response = intake confirmation text; escalation = timeout pager; Email-to-Case = faxed referral; Web-to-Case = kiosk form; default owner = charge nurse when protocols miss.
useful_mapping: Queue → shared bay, many clinicians can take work
Email-to-Case → inbound mailbox becomes a chart
Web-to-Case → public form creates a chart once
Support Settings default owner → charge nurse fallback
where_it_breaks: Manual Case create may skip assignment unless the user checks the assignment checkbox (Classic/LEX behavior—reverify UI).
Omni-Channel (APP-004) can take work from queues using capacity, which a static assignment rule does not.
Milestones are entitlement SLAs, not escalation rules.
The ER does not encode Experience Cloud login or Knowledge.

teach_back_prompt: Explain assignment versus auto-response versus escalation to a developer who wants one Flow for all three, then say when Email-to-Case beats Web-to-Case.

review_schedule.prompt: Name the six tools in this title and one sentence each.

Two-minute interview: Case routing without naming Omni-Channel as the only answer.

claims.claim: Assignment rules use record attributes to assign a record to a user or a queue. Multiple rules may exist; only one assignment rule can be active at a time for an object in the cited IT Services Help.

Web-to-Case is for initial case submission. Prerequisites include queues (if used), Support Settings default owner, and an active assignment rule. Over the daily limit, the default case owner is emailed the extra information.
Milestones on entitlement processes are time-dependent support steps such as first response or resolution. They are not assignment rules and are owned by APP-004.

changed_in_release: Reverify Email-to-Case On-Demand vs agent, Web-to-Case daily cap, and Case assignment checkbox behavior against Summer '26 Help.
unresolved_uncertainty: Numeric Web-to-Case daily limit should be read from current Help or org limits—do not quote an unofficial number.
Whether Lightning Case create applies assignment rules by default varies by UI; confirm in the target org.

interview_explanation.thirty_seconds: A Case is the work. Queues share it. Assignment rules pick user or queue at create. Auto-response emails the customer. Escalation waits, then notifies or reassigns. Email-to-Case and Web-to-Case are capture. Missed rules go to the default owner.
interview_explanation.two_minutes: I start from the channel. Email thread: Email-to-Case. One-shot form: Web-to-Case plus active assignment or Support Settings owner. Customer must come back: portal, not another form. I never use escalation as a thank-you email or auto-response as a late pager. Omni-Channel is APP-004 capacity routing sitting on queues. Milestones are entitlement clocks, not this rule type.

terminology.plain: A support work record: something the customer needs resolved.
terminology.precise: Standard Service object created manually, via Email-to-Case, Web-to-Case, or APIs. Owner may be a user or a queue.
terminology.example: LAB_Case 00001012 Origin Web, Status New, owned by LAB_Tier1 queue.
terminology.non_example: An Opportunity used as a 'support deal.'
terminology.confusable_neighbor: Work Order / Incident in other clouds: neighboring objects, not this lesson's Case.
terminology.boundary: Omni-Channel work items can include cases; routing design is APP-004.

terminology.plain: A shared inbox that can own Cases (and some other objects).
terminology.precise: Metadata: members and supported objects. Assignment rules often target queues. Not a User, though OwnerId points at the queue.
terminology.example: LAB_Tier1 queue with three agents as members.
terminology.non_example: A public Chatter group used as the only 'queue.'
terminology.confusable_neighbor: Omni-Channel queue: can be backed by the same queue with capacity (APP-004).
terminology.boundary: Lead queues exist too (APP-001); this lesson focuses on Case.

terminology.plain: Triage: put this new Case on that person or that shared bay.
terminology.precise: Criteria-based routing to a user or queue. Only one assignment rule should be active for the object (IT Services Help). Web cases without an active rule go to the default owner.
terminology.example: Origin = Email and Subject contains VIP → user LAB_Aarav.
terminology.non_example: An escalation that fires four hours later.
terminology.confusable_neighbor: Auto-response: emails the customer, does not set owner.
terminology.boundary: Flow can also assign; AUTO-001 decides when Flow is justified.

terminology.plain: The timeout pager if the Case sits too long.
terminology.precise: Time-based actions (notify, reassign) using business hours. Not the create-time thank-you. Not an entitlement milestone.
terminology.example: Priority High still New after 2 business hours → notify LAB_supervisor.
terminology.confusable_neighbor: Milestone: entitlement process clock (APP-004), up to 10 per process.
terminology.boundary: Do not invent exact default timers; they are configured.

terminology.plain: The 'we got your request' email when the Case is created.
terminology.precise: Criteria-based email at create. Requires email templates. Does not replace assignment.
terminology.non_example: A four-hour late notification (that is escalation).
terminology.boundary: Deliverability and org-wide email addresses are neighboring admin work.

terminology.plain: A mailbox that becomes Cases, usually keeping the email thread.
terminology.precise: Inbound email capture. Setup includes routing addresses. Different from a one-shot web form. On-Demand versus on-premises agent: reverify current Help.
terminology.example: support@lab.example creates Case LAB_00001020 with the message body.
terminology.non_example: Web-to-Case HTML posted from a marketing page.
terminology.boundary: Attachment size and threading limits: Needs verification per org.

terminology.plain: A public form that creates a Case once.
terminology.precise: Initial submission only. Needs default owner, preferably an active assignment rule, optional queues, and a response template. Over daily limit, extra submissions email the default owner instead of unlimited inserts.
terminology.example: LAB_ website 'Contact Support' form creates Origin=Web cases.
terminology.non_example: A logged-in Experience Cloud case publisher for follow-ups.
terminology.confusable_neighbor: Web-to-Lead: creates Leads, 500/day documented in APP-001.
terminology.boundary: Numeric Case daily cap: Needs verification; do not quote an unofficial figure.

terminology.plain: The charge nurse: who gets work when rules miss or limits hit.
terminology.precise: Set in Support Settings. Used when assignment is inactive or does not match, and when Web-to-Case exceeds its daily limit (email of leftover details).
terminology.non_example: Assuming the form 'failed' because the default owner has the case.
terminology.confusable_neighbor: Default lead owner in Lead Settings (APP-001).
terminology.boundary: Who monitors that mailbox/user is an operating-model choice.

interview_questions.question: How do Cases, queues, and assignment rules work together?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: A Case is the work. A Queue is shared ownership. An assignment rule uses criteria to send a new Case to a user or queue. Only one assignment rule should be active. Misses go to the default owner.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I set Support Settings first so overflow has a human. I create queues for teams. I activate one assignment rule with ordered entries. I do not confuse that with auto-response or escalation. Web-to-Case and Email-to-Case still depend on this routing. Omni-Channel can later pull from the same queues using capacity.
interview_questions.example: LAB_ web case Origin=Web → LAB_Tier1 queue; Subject VIP → Aarav.
follow_ups: Does manual create run the rule?

interview_questions.question: Email-to-Case versus Web-to-Case?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Email-to-Case turns mailbox threads into Cases. Web-to-Case is a public form for the first submit only. Both still need assignment or a default owner.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I pick Email-to-Case when customers already write email and need replies on the thread. I pick Web-to-Case for anonymous marketing-site forms. I refuse Web-to-Case as a portal. I mention daily-limit overflow emails the default owner, without inventing the number. Attachments and spam controls differ; I reverify current Help.
interview_questions.example: support@lab.example versus the LAB_ Contact Support form.
tradeoffs: Spam on email vs bot on forms
weak_answer_warnings: Treating them as the same feature

interview_questions.question: Customer never got a thank-you but the Case exists. Walk it.
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Check auto-response rule, criteria, template, and deliverability. Do not look at escalation first; that is a later clock.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I confirm Origin and whether Email-to-Case already sent a different path. I check the rule is active. I look at bounce reports. I do not build a Flow until the standard auto-response is proven wrong. If they wanted a late warning, that is escalation or a milestone, not auto-response.
interview_questions.example: Origin Phone case, auto-response only for Origin Web.

interview_questions.question: VIP High cases sit four hours. Design the clock.
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Use an escalation rule with business hours to notify or reassign. If they need contractual first-response SLAs, that is entitlements and milestones in APP-004.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I do not add a Stage-like Status for 'waiting.' I set criteria Priority High and Status New. I pick actions. I warn that assignment rules do not re-run on a timer. If they already bought Entitlement Management, I do not duplicate clocks blindly.
interview_questions.example: LAB_ High case escalates to LAB_supervisor after 2 business hours.

interview_questions.question: All web cases hit the admin. Diagnose.
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Assignment rule inactive or entries do not match. Then the default owner is working as designed. Check the form hidden fields too.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I compare a LAB_ submit's field values to rule entries. I confirm only one rule is active. I look at Support Settings. I check daily-limit overflow emails versus created cases. I do not regenerate HTML first unless the org ID on the form is wrong.
interview_questions.example: Rule requires Origin = Email but Web-to-Case sets Origin Web.
tradeoffs: Fix criteria vs change default owner
follow_ups: Is the form pointing at the right org?
weak_answer_warnings: Regenerating HTML as the only step

interview_questions.question: Web form users ask where to 'log in to their case.'
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Web-to-Case cannot do that. Offer an authenticated Experience Cloud or similar portal. Keep the form for first submit only.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I quote the official 'initial submission' limit. I separate capture from self-service. I do not promise case status on a second public form. Knowledge and console come later (APP-004). I still keep assignment and auto-response on the first Case.
interview_questions.example: LAB_ form creates the Case; customers later use LAB_ community login.
weak_answer_warnings: Building a second public form as a portal

interview_questions.question: When would you still write a Flow for Case assignment?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: When assignment-rule criteria cannot express the logic (complex related records, callouts, or updates after create). I still keep default owner and queues.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: AUTO-001 owns the tool choice. I do not replace a working first-match rule with Flow for sport. Escalation and auto-response remain standard unless we need richer branching. Omni-Channel may remove the need for clever assignment if the real problem is agent capacity.
interview_questions.example: Assign using related Account SLA field that assignment-rule entry cannot see—Needs verification; then Flow or entitlement.
follow_ups: Who debugs the Flow at 2 a.m.?

interview_questions.question: Teach this ER analogy and where it breaks.
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Case is the chart, queue the bay, assignment the triage, auto-response the intake text, escalation the timeout pager, email the fax, web the kiosk, default owner the charge nurse.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: It breaks when manual create skips the triage checkbox, when Omni-Channel becomes the dispatcher, and when milestones are the contractual clocks. I cite one-active-rule, default owner, daily-limit email, and 'not a portal.' I keep LAB_ data in the story.
interview_questions.example: Whiteboard: two channels, one active rule, one default owner, two clocks.
weak_answer_warnings: Generic catalog metaphors instead of the hospital-desk mapping
